findings.finding: The search part of §3 points at the wrong mechanism. Its condition is met, because `search` already exposes `--has-tag` (reads_cli.py:531, 544, 572), so the plan commits to `search --release`. But search never calls `apply_ticket_filters`: its keyword filters run in `compile_search` (reducer/search.py:163-198, a single exact `has_tag` check, not comma-OR), threaded through `search_state` (_engine_support/reads.py:565-598), `_lib_reads.search` and `_reads.search`. It also has its own `_SEARCH_VALUE_OPTS` and `_search_prefix` allowlists (reads_cli.py:114, 531). None of these are in Scope and no test covers search. The codebase also has a better hook the plan does not use: `match_predicate` in reducer/_filters.py is documented as 'the single comparison vocabulary shared by the structured-query parser and apply_ticket_filters', and `_query.KNOWN_FIELDS` lists `tag`. Adding a `release` field there (a `_match_release` beside `_match_tag`, plus `release` in KNOWN_FIELDS) would let one matcher serve `list --release` and `search 'release:2.4'`, with the same exact-name, comma-OR, no-inheritance rules.
findings.location: Approach §3 — "(and on `search` if `search` already exposes `--has-tag`)"; reducer/_filters.py `apply_ticket_filters`
scenarios: Following the plan, an implementer adds `--release` to build_search and reads_cli line 544, but `search_state`/`compile_search` take no release argument, so the flag is dropped or causes a TypeError.
`search` ends up with exact single-value release matching while `list --release` uses comma-OR, and `search 'release:2.4'` silently becomes a substring search.
findings.suggested_fix: In §3, say that `release_filter` evaluates `match_predicate(t, "release", "in", values)` through a new `_match_release` (any-of over `state.get("releases") or []`), and add `"release"` to `reducer/_query.py` KNOWN_FIELDS so `rebar search 'release:2.4'` works through the shared vocabulary. Replace the conditional `search --release` clause with that, add `reducer/_query.py` to Scope, document `release:` in search.txt, and add one search test.
